content: If these signs persist for more than a few days, it strongly suggests that the adolescent may require additional support. Say, We all need to take care of both our physical and mental health. Write or draw three things you do to maintain your physical health. Then, write or draw three things you do to take care of your mental health. After a few minutes, ask, Does anyone feel comfortable sharing their ideas? If so, please come and write or draw them here. Say, Would anyone like to share a story about a time when they tried these strategies? Recognize how you are feeling. Be kind to yourself. Engage in activities that you enjoy or that bring you a sense of accomplishment. Connect with your loved ones. Talk about your feelings with someone you trust. Seek help from a trusted individual or a professional if you feel stuck or overwhelmed. Step 4: Revision of main concepts (1 minute) Say, Thank you, everyone. Today, we’ve spent time learning about the importance of taking care of our physical and mental health. It is crucial to recognize the signals our body and mind give us when we experience certain emotions. By doing so, we can identify when to seek additional help from someone we trust or reach out to a friend who may need support. This helps us better understand ourselves and the people around us. Step 5: Practice (4 minutes) Say, I’d like all of you to write or draw three signs you notice in yourself when your emotions start to feel too intense or overwhelming. What are these feelings? Then, write or draw three things you can do to help yourself. Be sure to include talking to someone you trust, such as a trusted adult or friend. You don’t need to show this to anyone else. It’s just for you. You do not need to ask to see their list or check if they completed it. It is entirely up to the students to decide whether they want to do it.
